title: Gemini Omni Flash
summary: Google's video generation and editing model on the Gemini API, with audio.
why_it_matters: It is the replacement Google names for Veo 3.1 on the Gemini API.
fit_notes: Paid tier only, so it cannot be tried for free. Priced in output tokens; the per-second figures are Google's own approximation.

claims.text: Google prices 720p output at about $0.07 per second, so a 10 second clip is about $0.70.
claims.quote: approximately $0.07 per second (~$0.70 for a 10s clip, ~$1.04 for a 15s clip;
claims.locator: Gemini API pricing page, section Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash

claims.text: It generates and edits up to 15 seconds of video with audio, on the paid tier only.
claims.quote: up to 15 seconds of video generation and editing with native audio, now generally available to developers on the paid tier of the Gemini API.
claims.locator: Gemini API pricing page, section Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash

checked.what: Gemini API pricing page against both claims

title: Veo 3.1
summary: Google's video generation model. It was removed from the Gemini API in October 2026.
why_it_matters: Code and skills that call Veo through the Gemini API need to migrate.
fit_notes: Whether it stays available on Google's enterprise platform or through resellers was not checked.
status_note: Left the Gemini API 2026-10-22. Other access routes not checked.

claims.text: The Gemini API lists a shutdown date of 2026-10-22 for veo-3.1-generate-preview and names gemini-omni-1.2-flash as the replacement.

checked.what: Gemini API deprecations page against the claim

title: MiniMax H3
summary: An open-weights video generation model from MiniMax, also sold through its API.
why_it_matters: A leading open-weights video model whose licence does not cover several major regions.
fit_notes: Read the licence for where you are before using the weights. Ports for Apple Silicon exist, but the one published timing is minutes per denoising step on a larger machine, and nothing was measured here.

claims.text: The licence defines the EU, the UK, South Korea and the USA as excluded territories.
claims.quote: “Excluded Territories” means the European Union, the United Kingdom, the Republic of Korea and the United States of America.

claims.text: The licence applies worldwide except those territories.
claims.quote: “Applicable Territory” means worldwide, excluding the Excluded Territories.

checked.what: LICENSE file on the model repository against both claims

title: Sora 2
summary: OpenAI's video generation model family. Its API access ended in September 2026.
why_it_matters: Many guides and skills still call it. Anything that depends on the Videos API no longer runs.
fit_notes: Do not build on it. The deprecations entry lists no replacement model.
status_note: API removed 2026-09-24 per OpenAI's deprecations page.

claims.text: OpenAI removed the Sora 2 models and the Videos API from its API on 2026-09-24.
claims.quote: On March 24th, 2026, we notified developers using the Videos API and Sora 2 video generation model aliases and snapshots of their deprecation and removal from the API on September 24, 2026.

checked.what: OpenAI deprecations page against the claim

title: Remotion's Model Context Protocol (shut down)
summary: Remotion's notice that it closed its hosted MCP server and moved users to its Agent Skills, with reasons.
why_it_matters: A vendor's own account of choosing skills over an MCP server for code-driven video.
fit_notes: One vendor's experience with a documentation server. Hosted render and generation vendors still lead with MCP.

claims.text: Remotion shut down its hosted MCP server on 2026-10-26.
claims.quote: The hosted Remotion MCP server was shut down on October 26, 2026

claims.text: Among its stated reasons: MCP servers were hard to install and agents did not call them reliably.
claims.quote: Installing MCP servers was difficult, and agents did not invoke them reliably.
claims.locator: section Why was the MCP shut down?

checked.what: Remotion docs page against both claims

title: video-use
summary: A skill for cutting raw footage into a finished video by conversation, with hard audio and cut rules and a self-evaluation pass on the rendered file.
why_it_matters: The clearest example of a skill that inspects its own output at every cut before handing it over.
fit_notes: Transcription uses a paid ElevenLabs key, so it is not a free local path as shipped. Its README tells the agent to ask you to paste the key into chat; set it in the environment yourself.

claims.text: It forbids cutting inside a word and snaps cuts to transcript word boundaries.
claims.quote: **Never cut inside a word.** Snap every cut edge to a word boundary from the Scribe transcript.

title: claude-code-video-toolkit
summary: A Claude Code workspace of skills, slash commands and Python tools for script to voiceover to visuals to MP4. Its video-design skill fixes type, alignment and colour rules.
why_it_matters: Its design rules address the most common amateur tells: wrapped titles, drifting alignment, colour changes with no reason.
fit_notes: Claude Code only as stated. The quick start needs no API keys; its AI tools run on your own cloud GPU account.

claims.text: Its design skill bounds the review loop at three rounds.

title: claude-remotion-skill
summary: A Remotion motion-graphics skill with non-negotiable easing, stagger and exit rules and a mandatory render, extract frames, inspect, fix loop.
why_it_matters: Adds the frame-inspection step the official Remotion skills leave to a person.
fit_notes: Two of its rules (idle elements breathe; never a flat background) contradict the HyperFrames and video-design skills. Pick one rule set per project.

claims.text: It bans linear interpolation in every composition.

title: HyperFrames
summary: An HTML and GSAP video renderer with a skill pack. The agent writes a page, the CLI captures it frame by frame and encodes MP4.
why_it_matters: One of the two renderers most agent-made video runs on, and its skill carries numeric motion, review and loudness rules.
fit_notes: Start here for a fully local render with no licence fee. The skill asks the agent to send a usage beacon through the CLI at start; read the skill before installing if that matters to you. Hosted media features need a HeyGen sign-in.

claims.text: Its motion reference tells the agent not to reuse one ease and duration for every element.
claims.quote: The same `power2.out` at 0.5 s on everything is the flat default that makes a film feel generated.

claims.text: It sets exits shorter than entrances by a stated ratio.

checked.what: motion.md in the skill folder against both claims

title: Remotion Agent Skills
summary: The official skill set for writing Remotion (React) video with a coding agent: creation, markup, captions, rendering.
why_it_matters: The reference skills for the other dominant renderer. They state support for Codex and Cursor as well as Claude Code.
fit_notes: The skills repo has no licence file, and Remotion itself has a company licence: check both before client work. The skill opens a preview for a person; it does not make the agent inspect frames.

claims.text: Its layout rule keeps key text inside a stated safe area.
claims.quote: For 1080px-wide videos, keep key text at least 80px from the sides and 100px from the top and bottom.

claims.text: It asks for one focal point per scene.
claims.quote: Decide what the viewer should notice first in each scene. Build the frame around that one thing.

checked.what: video-layout.md in the remotion-create skill against both claims

title: video-shotcraft
summary: A product-promo skill built on shot-recipe cards and real page captures, written in Chinese, stating support for Claude Code and Codex.
why_it_matters: It makes the reviewer a different agent from the maker, which is the strongest review-loop rule found so far.
fit_notes: The repo is four months old with a high star count; treat popularity as unconfirmed. Needs network for page capture and sound search. Instructions are in Chinese.

claims.text: Before delivery it requires an independent final review by a sub-agent with a clean context.
claims.quote: 交付前必须派一个干净上下文的 subagent 做独立终检
